John Kemp Starley 1854 - 1901
In 1885 in Coventry, Starley made history
when he produced the Rover Safety Bicycle,
a chain driven bicycle with similar sized wheels.

Edward Langley Fardon 1839 - 1926
An accomplished whitesmith and engineer, he
produced one of the most significant evolutions to
the deign of the modern bicycle

Helen Martin 1907 - 1988
Set up a charitable trust to help
the University of Warwick, its total
contribution to date is
£28 Million

Find out more about these local people at
www.sustrans.org.uk/portraitbench


The characters for this Portrait Bench chosen by your community
celebrate
Sustrans
winning a nationwide vote in 2007
to create new walking and cycling routes
across the UK, funded by
the Big Lottery Fund

C. S. Lewis
In the opening scenes of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe heroine Lucy meets faun Mr Tümnus under a gas lamp in a snowy woodland.

Author C. S. Lewis studied at Malvern College, and visited Malvern as an adult too. Gas lamps were more common then, but Malvern is rare
today in having so many surviving lamps in use. Whether or not Lewis
was inspired by gas lamps on the wooded paths to Malvern's hills, they certainly create an atmospheric spot where even now you can easily imagine yourself in Narnia heritage

One night a man had a dream. He dreamed he was
walking along the beach with the Lord. Across the
sky flashed scenes from his life. For each scene, he
noticed two sets of footprints in the sand: one
belonging to him. and the other to the Lord. When
the last scene of his life flashed before him, he
looked back at the footprints in the sand. He
noticed that many times along the path of his life
there was only one set of footprints. He also noticed
that it happened at the very lowest and saddest
times in his life. This really bothered him and he
questioned the Lord about it. "Lord, You said that
once I decided to follow you, You'd walk with me all
the way. But I have noticed that during the most
troublesome times in my life, there is only one set
of footprints. I don't understand why when I needed
you most you would leave me." The Lord replied,
"My son. My precious child. I love you and I would
never leave you. During your times of trial and
suffering when you see only one set of footprints, it
was then that carried you."

Richard Charles Lewis Bradshaw
30th September 1944 – 18th January 2014
Richard moved to Redditch in 1979.
He influenced and inspired others to improve their general health, fitness and cycling skills.
He joined the now Cycling Touring Club CTC Heart of England Cycling Club in 1999.
He was a Founder Member of Redditch & Bromsgrove CTC Cycling Club.
He became a Sustrans Volunteer Ranger from 2011 and a Sustrans Group Co-ordinator from 2012.
He started the Sustrans led rides from Arrow Valley Park in 2013 to encourage residents to use the local infrastructure for safer cycling of routes to school, the shops and work.
He became a Bikeability Instructor in October 2012 training children in local primary schools about cycling road safety.
He led a group of volunteers to audit potential cycle routes in and around Redditch for the 'Choose How You Move' Project.
Richard's dedication to cycling has been honoured by naming this bridge 'The Richard Bradshaw Bridge'.

Our Special Man
Although we cannot touch you or hear you call our name, the
memories we have of you will never ever fade.
You put smiles upon our faces and warmth in our hearts, the love
that we share for you will never ever part.
Words cannot be written to explain the utter pain,
of you not being here with us today.
Grandad, like a dad to me you were, that bond will never fade,
and the love I have for you will never blow away.
I thought of you today, but that is nothing new,
I will think of you tomorrow and every day after too.
We thought of you yesterday and the days before that too,
we think of you in silence with a smile or two.
The memories we hold of you and photos in a frame,
Such a handsome man you were and always very vain.
Fishing trips to the lake was always your favourite place
with Joan and Bonbons by your side
as you sat and watched the days pass by.
Since you have been taken far far away,
rest in peace in harmony as you now lay,
without any pain or suffering in your soul,
until the day we meet again our hearts will not be whole.
Dad, Grandad, Bernie and Great Grandad,
rest in peace angel, we love you,
always and forever our special man.
Poem by Charlene Robbins (Granddaughter)
